hero.title: Express Entry — Federal Skilled Worker Program
hero.subtitle: Canada's flagship immigration system for skilled workers. Create a profile, enter the pool, and receive an Invitation to Apply based on your CRS score.

requirements.title: Do You Qualify?
qualifications: At least 1 year of continuous skilled work experience (NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3)
Language skills meeting CLB 7 or higher in all four abilities
A post-secondary credential or Canadian equivalent via ECA
Sufficient settlement funds (varies by family size)
No criminal record and passing a medical examination

steps.title: The Express Entry Process
steps.subtitle: From creating your profile to receiving your permanent residence.

items.title: Create Your Profile
items.description: Submit your Express Entry profile via the IRCC portal with your work experience, education, and language test results.

items.title: Enter the Pool
items.description: Your profile is ranked in the Express Entry pool against other candidates using the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS).

items.title: Receive an ITA
items.description: IRCC holds regular draws and issues Invitations to Apply (ITAs) to the highest-ranked candidates.

items.title: Submit Your PR Application
items.description: You have 60 days to submit a complete permanent residence application with all supporting documents.

items.title: Receive Permanent Residence
items.description: Most Express Entry applications are processed within 6 months of submission.

items.title: Federal Skilled Worker (FSW)
items.description: For workers with foreign skilled work experience and a strong CRS score. Requires an ECA for foreign credentials.

items.title: Canadian Experience Class (CEC)
items.description: For workers who already have at least 1 year of Canadian skilled work experience in the last 3 years.

items.title: Federal Skilled Trades (FST)
items.description: For workers in skilled trade occupations with a job offer or certificate of qualification in Canada.

cta.title: What Is Your CRS Score?
cta.subtitle: Calculate your score in 2 minutes and see how you compare to recent Express Entry draws.

hero.title: Study in Canada
hero.subtitle: Gain a Canadian education, work during your studies, and build a clear path to permanent residence through the Post-Graduation Work Permit.

requirements.title: Key Requirements
qualifications: An acceptance letter from a Designated Learning Institution (DLI) in Canada
Proof of sufficient funds (minimum CAD $20,635/year for living costs plus tuition)
Language scores meeting your program's requirements (typically IELTS 6.0+ or equivalent)
No criminal record and passing a medical examination if required
Proof that you will comply with the conditions of your permit

steps.title: How to Get Your Study Permit

items.title: Choose a Designated Learning Institution
items.description: Select a DLI-approved school in Canada and receive your letter of acceptance before applying.

items.title: Apply for a Study Permit
items.description: Submit your study permit application online via IRCC with your acceptance letter, financial proof, and language scores.

items.title: Receive Your Permit
items.description: Once approved, you will receive a Port of Entry letter of introduction to present at the Canadian border.

items.title: Arrive and Start Your Studies
items.description: Present your documents at the border. You can work 20 hours per week during the academic semester and full-time during breaks.

items.title: Work While You Study
items.description: Study permit holders can work up to 20 hours per week during the academic semester and full-time during scheduled breaks.

items.title: Post-Graduation Work Permit
items.description: After graduating, you may be eligible for a PGWP of up to 3 years — giving you time to gain the Canadian experience needed for CEC.

items.title: Clear Path to Permanent Residence
items.description: Just 1 year of Canadian skilled work after graduation makes you eligible for the Canadian Experience Class — one of the fastest PR routes.

hero.title: Work in Canada
hero.subtitle: A Canadian work permit lets you gain valuable experience, build your CRS score, and create a pathway to permanent residence.

requirements.title: Do You Qualify?
qualifications: A valid job offer from a Canadian employer (for LMIA-based permits)
Your employer has received a positive Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA), or your role is LMIA-exempt
You meet the language and educational requirements for your occupation
No criminal record and passing a medical examination if required
You qualify under CUSMA, the International Experience Canada (IEC) program, or an intra-company transfer (for LMIA-exempt)

steps.title: How to Get a Work Permit

items.title: Secure a Job Offer
items.description: Find a Canadian employer willing to hire you. For LMIA-based permits, they must first obtain a positive LMIA from ESDC.

items.title: Determine Your Permit Type
items.description: Confirm whether your role requires an LMIA or qualifies for an exemption (CUSMA, intra-company transfer, IEC).

items.title: Apply for Your Work Permit
items.description: Submit your work permit application online via IRCC with your job offer letter, LMIA number (if applicable), and supporting documents.

items.title: Build Canadian Experience
items.description: Work in Canada, gain 1+ year of skilled work experience, and become eligible for the Canadian Experience Class in Express Entry.

items.title: LMIA-Based Permit
items.description: Your employer applies for a Labour Market Impact Assessment proving no qualified Canadian was available for the role.

items.title: CUSMA / NAFTA Permit
items.description: For citizens of USA and Mexico in specific professional occupations. No LMIA required — faster processing at the border.

items.title: Intra-Company Transfer
items.description: For employees of multinational companies transferring to a Canadian office in a managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge role.

hero.title: Reunite With Your Family in Canada
hero.subtitle: If you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, you can sponsor eligible family members to become permanent residents of Canada.

requirements.title: Who Can You Sponsor?
qualifications: Your spouse, common-law partner, or conjugal partner
Your dependent children (under 22 years old, not married or in a common-law relationship)
Your parents and grandparents (through the Parents and Grandparents Program)
Other relatives in specific circumstances (e.g., orphaned siblings, nephews, nieces)
You must be 18 or older, a Canadian citizen or PR, and meet the minimum income requirement

items.title: Confirm Eligibility
items.description: Verify that you meet the sponsor requirements (age, status, income) and that your family member is eligible to be sponsored.

items.title: Submit Sponsorship Application
items.description: Submit both your sponsorship application and your family member's permanent residence application at the same time to IRCC.

items.title: Biometrics & Medical Exam
items.description: Your family member will be required to provide biometrics and complete an immigration medical examination.

items.title: Background Checks
items.description: IRCC conducts security and criminal background checks on your family member as part of the admissibility assessment.

items.title: Receive Permanent Residence
items.description: Once approved, your family member will receive their Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and can land in Canada.

items.title: Spouse & Partner Sponsorship
items.description: Sponsor your spouse, common-law partner (12 months cohabitation), or conjugal partner. Processing takes approximately 12 months.

items.title: Dependent Child Sponsorship
items.description: Sponsor your dependent children under 22 who are not married or in a common-law relationship. Biological, adopted, and step-children may qualify.

items.title: Parents & Grandparents Program
items.description: Apply through the annual PGP lottery to sponsor parents and grandparents. Super Visas are also available as a temporary alternative.

hero.title: Provincial Nominee Program (PNP)
hero.subtitle: A provincial nomination adds 600 points to your CRS score — virtually guaranteeing an Invitation to Apply at the next Express Entry draw.

requirements.title: Do You Qualify?
qualifications: Skills, education, or work experience that meets a specific province's labour market needs
An intention to live and work in the nominating province
You meet federal admissibility requirements (health, security, language)
You are already in the Express Entry pool (for Enhanced PNP streams)
Some streams require a job offer or a prior connection to the province

items.title: Choose Your Target Province
items.description: Research which provinces have streams matching your occupation, education, and experience. Each province has different requirements.

items.title: Apply to the Provincial Program
items.description: Submit a provincial application directly or via an Express Entry enhanced stream. Many provinces have their own Expression of Interest systems.

items.title: Receive Your Nomination
items.description: If selected, the province nominates you. For Express Entry PNP streams, IRCC immediately adds 600 CRS points to your profile.

items.title: Apply for Permanent Residence
items.description: With 600 extra CRS points you are virtually guaranteed an ITA at the next draw. Submit your PR application within 60 days.

items.title: Ontario (OINP)
items.description: Canada's largest province offers streams for tech workers, in-demand trades, and international students from Ontario universities.

items.title: British Columbia (BC PNP)
items.description: Strong tech sector with dedicated streams for software engineers, data scientists, and health professionals.

items.title: Alberta (AINP)
items.description: Growing economy with streams for the Alberta Advantage, rural renewal, and self-employed farmers.

hero.title: Tourist Visa (TRV) for Canada
hero.subtitle: Planning to visit Canada? Our certified consultants prepare a complete, compelling application to give you the best chance of approval.

requirements.title: Do You Need a Tourist Visa?
qualifications: You are a citizen of a country that requires a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) to enter Canada
You plan to visit Canada for tourism, family visits, or short business trips (up to 6 months)
You have a valid passport and sufficient funds to cover your stay
You can demonstrate strong ties to your home country (employment, property, family)
You have no criminal record and meet all Canadian admissibility requirements
You have a clear purpose of visit and intent to return home after your stay

items.title: Eligibility Assessment
items.description: We review your travel history, ties to your home country, financial situation, and purpose of visit to assess your approval chances.

items.title: Document Preparation
items.description: We provide a personalised checklist and review every document — bank statements, employment letters, itinerary, invitation letters — for completeness.

items.title: Application Submission
items.description: We prepare and review your IMM 5257 form, cover letter, and supporting documents, then guide you through the online submission process.

items.title: Biometrics & Interview Support
items.description: We guide you through biometrics enrolment and prepare you for any potential visa officer interview or additional document requests.

items.title: Tailored Cover Letter
items.description: A professional cover letter addressing your specific situation, ties to home, and purpose of visit significantly increases approval rates.

items.title: Document Review
items.description: Our consultants review all supporting documents for gaps, inconsistencies, or missing information before submission.

items.title: Refusal Assistance
items.description: Previously refused? We analyse the refusal reasons, strengthen your application, and guide you through a new submission.
